工业生态学中的物质流分析(MFA)如何刻画经济系统的“代谢”结构?以铜或磷为例,它能带来哪些政策层面的启示?

In industrial ecology, how does material flow analysis (MFA) map the 'metabolism' of an economy, and what policy insights emerge when it is applied to copper or phosphorus?

物质流分析沿开采、加工、使用、废弃各环节追踪元素的存量和流量,把经济体当作一个代谢系统审视:在用库存越大,将来形成的报废流就越可观。铜的多层循环研究表明,全球社会在用库存已达人均约一百公斤量级且报废流持续扩张,提高再生利用率比单纯扩产矿山更能缓解原生资源与供应风险。磷的账户则揭示矿山—农田—水体之间的单向漏损及其引发的富营养化,据此应将从污泥和厨余中回收磷列为政策优先事项。
Material flow analysis follows an element's stocks and flows through extraction, processing, use and disposal, treating the economy as a metabolic system: the larger the in-use stock, the larger the eventual end-of-life flows. Multilevel copper studies find global in-use stocks on the order of one hundred kilograms per capita with steadily growing scrap flows, so raising recycling rates eases pressure on primary supply more effectively than opening new mines alone. Phosphorus accounts expose the one-way leakage along the mine-farm-water pathway and the eutrophication it causes, which argues for prioritizing phosphorus recovery from sewage sludge and food waste.

生物基塑料（如 PLA）一定比石油塑料更环保吗？

Are bio-based plastics like PLA necessarily greener than petroleum plastics?

不一定。PLA 需要工业堆肥高温条件才能降解，混入普通回收会污染料流；其原料种植还涉及土地、化肥与水的代价，需全生命周期评估才能下结论。
Not necessarily. PLA needs industrial-compost high temperatures to degrade and contaminates conventional recycling; feedstock farming carries land, fertilizer and water costs, so life-cycle assessment is needed.

电子产品的“模块化设计”如何促进循环？

How does modular design of electronics promote circularity?

把电池、屏幕、芯片等做成可单独更换的模块，便于维修、升级与回收，延长产品寿命并提高稀有金属的回收效率，减少整机废弃。
Making batteries, screens and chips individually replaceable eases repair, upgrades and recovery, extends product life and improves rare-metal recycling, cutting whole-device waste.

旧物“维修权（right to repair）”为什么被写进环保法规？

Why is the 'right to repair' written into environmental law?

过去厂家用专用件、加密芯片和禁修条款逼你换新，制造大量电子垃圾；保障用户和第三方维修，能延长产品寿命、减少废弃与碳排，是循环经济的制度支点。
Makers once used proprietary parts, crypto-chips and no-repair clauses to force replacements, making e-waste; guaranteeing user and third-party repair extends life and cuts waste and carbon—a pillar of circularity.

循环经济为什么强调再使用与再制造要优先于材料回收？

Why does the circular economy give reuse and remanufacturing priority over material recycling?

循环经济按“内环优先”排序价值保留策略：维护修理、再使用、再制造等内层循环保留产品的结构与加工中蕴含的能耗，只需少量投入即可恢复功能；而回收把产品打回材料形态，常伴随品质降级——例如混合塑料只能降级利用——并损失大部分隐含能源。循环离原始用户越近，节材、节能与减排的效果就越好。
Circular-economy strategy ranks value-retention options by how much embedded value they keep. Inner loops such as maintenance and repair, direct reuse, and remanufacturing preserve a product's structure and the energy invested in shaping its parts, so little input restores full function. Recycling, by contrast, reduces products back to materials, usually with quality loss—mixed plastics, for instance, can only be downcycled—and forfeits most embodied processing energy. The closer a loop stays to the original user, the greater the savings in material, energy, and emissions.

循环经济和普通的“回收”本质区别在哪？

What is the essential difference between circular economy and ordinary recycling?

回收多在末端处理废弃物；循环经济从设计端就“消除废物与污染、让材料和产品持续循环、并主动修复自然”，追求源头减量与再利用，而非事后补救。
Recycling treats waste at the end; circular economy designs out waste and pollution from the start, keeps materials and products in use, and regenerates nature—prevention and reuse over after-the-fact fixes.

什么是“维修权”（right to repair）运动？

What is the 'right to repair' movement?

它主张消费者和独立维修店应能获得备件、图纸和诊断工具，打破厂商垄断维修。延长产品寿命、减少电子废物是核心目标。
It argues consumers and independent shops should access parts, schematics and tools, breaking manufacturer repair monopolies. Extending product life and cutting e-waste are the core goals.
